Subject: Acme Corp - Redwood Bakeoff Discovery Recap & Next Steps

Thanks for taking the time today, Jordan and Samantha — great conversation. Quick recap of what we covered and the proposed next steps for the bakeoff so we can make sure we're aligned before kickoff.

Key pain points you described:
- High cost and variable latency from your current cloud endpoints when serving multi-turn assistant workloads.
- Unpredictable throughput during peak business hours (search+completion hybrid).
- Need for deterministic performance for SLAs on response times (p95 targets).

Current stack you shared:
- Inference: self-hosted vLLM for internal tests + managed cloud endpoints for prod (TGI and hosted cloud endpoints).
- Orchestration: K8s with autoscaling, custom batching layer.
- Observability: internal traces + Datadog.

Success criteria you asked us to validate in the bakeoff:
1) Latency: p95 for end-to-end generation under a realistic concurrency profile (target: <=150ms for single-turn 1k-token prompts; we'll capture multi-turn separately).
2) Throughput: sustain X requests/sec at 4k context with cold/warm cache scenarios.
3) Cost: estimated token-level cost comparison at production scale (monthly projection).
4) Functional parity: no more than a 2% delta in your evaluation metric on the 500-case prompt set you provided.
5) Reliability: graceful fallback behavior under capacity limits.

What Redwood will deliver for the bakeoff (proposal):
- A reproducible benchmark harness (load script + evaluation harness) and the suggested workload configs for our runtime.
- Guidance on model variants (FP16 vs quantized) and batching/KV cache settings for parity with vLLM/TGI setups.
- Baseline numbers from Redwood for the same prompt set and head-to-head comparison notes.

Requested items from Acme to run the customer-owned side of the test:
- Confirmation of the 500-prompt evaluation set (or a link to the dataset).
- Target concurrency profile (typical and 95th percentile peak).
- Any cost model inputs you want us to use for monthly projection (e.g., monthly tokens, expected live users).

Acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Redwood p95 latency <= 150ms (single-turn, 1k tokens) AND cost per 1M tokens <= current cloud endpoint baseline + 15% (or reduce cost).
- Functional delta <= 2% on your metric.

Next steps / timeline:
1) You confirm prompts and concurrency by EOD Thursday (10/15).
2) We provide bakeoff harness + config and propose dates for a 3-day run next week (10/19-10/21).
3) Joint validation of results and a short review meeting (30 mins) on 10/22.

Attachments: acme_bakeoff_requirements.pdf (summary of what we discussed), bakeoff_template.xlsx (benchmark matrix template).

If that aligns, we'll send a short calendar invite and the Drive link with the harness.

Best,

Hi Jordan — adding a few technical notes to help frame the comparison vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints and what we'll measure in the bakeoff.

Short comparison (high level):
- vLLM (self-hosted): strong single-node latency with aggressive KV cache reuse but can have breakdowns at scale without optimized batching/orchestration. Cold-starts average higher latency depending on provisioning.
- TGI/cloud endpoints: usually predictable but higher per-token overhead due to container/endpoint infra; less control over KV cache tuning.
- Redwood runtime: optimized kernel selection + continuous batching + KV-level prefix caching. Expect better warm p95 at scale and more deterministic tail latency due to smart routing and autoscaling policies.

What we'll measure in the harness:
- p50/p95/p99 latency for single-turn and multi-turn flows (1k / 4k context scenarios).
- Throughput under sustained load (8 req/s target) and a burst profile to simulate peak traffic.
- Cold vs warm cache performance (start of run vs after KV population).
- Token-level cost estimate using your inputs (we'll report normalized cost per 1M tokens).
- Quality/regression: we'll run your 500-case prompt set and report the evaluation metric you specify; please confirm exact metric (BLEU/Exact Match/custom script).

Recommended Redwood config for parity testing: model: rwd-llama2-13b (FP16), quantized variant for cost runs, batch_size 4, kv_cache_enabled: true, max_seq_len: 4096. We'll include a ready-to-run config file (redwood-bakeoff-config.yaml).

I'll attach the config file and a short comparison table. Happy to jump on a 30-min deep-dive with your infra team if helpful.

- Stephanie
